module purpose: neorv32_cache is a direct-mapped cache controller: it buffers host access strobes and fences, looks the host address up in the valid, tag and data arrays of its neorv32_cache_memory sub-unit, answers read hits with the cached word, downloads a whole block over the downstream bus on a read miss, passes uncached accesses (address at or above UC_BEGIN, atomic or debug) and writes through to the bus, clears all valid flags on a fence, and invalidates the block and returns an error when the download sees a bus error.

use-case flows.value: buffered host access strobe and fence request that begin a lookup or a cache clear
hit decision: the index and tag of the host address looked up in the valid and tag arrays
uncached (direct) access decision and pass-through of the bus transaction and its response
write handling: a write hit updates the cached word with the host byte enables and data and is written through to the bus; a write miss goes only to the bus
block download on a read miss: block address built from the captured tag, index and word offset, line allocated, each bus word written into the data array, offset counted to the end of the block
cached word returned to the host with an acknowledge on a read hit
download bus error accumulated, reported to the host as ack with err, and the block invalidated
controller state and buffers cleared while rstn_i is low; all valid flags cleared by rstn_i and by the fence clear command

conceptual assets.concept: Cached data -- the words of the cached blocks held in the data array and returned to the host on a read hit
conceptual assets.reasoning: The read-out flow returns the stored word: `rdata_o( 7 downto  0) <= data_mem_b0(to_integer(unsigned(acc_adr)));` (line 425, other bytes lines 426-428) reaches host_rsp_o.data through cache_i.data (lines 291, 156) and is acknowledged on a read hit (line 191). The array is written only by `data_mem_b0(to_integer(unsigned(acc_adr))) <= wdata_i(7 downto 0);` under we_i(0) (lines 413-414, other bytes lines 416-423), fed with host write data on a write hit (lines 151, 194) or with bus_rsp_i.data during a download (lines 236-237). Integrity: the word returned on a hit must equal the word last written for that block (lines 414, 425); a corrupted entry is answered as valid read data without any bus access. Availability is also established: the array holds each word between writes and returns it one clock edge after addressing (lines 412, 425). No line restricts who may read a cached word, so confidentiality is not established. data_mem_b0 to data_mem_b3 store (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 2); wdata_i sets (SOURCES data_mem_b0, occurrence 2), read by neorv32_cache_memory to store; rdata_o is the exit port of neorv32_cache_memory (DERIVES_FROM data_mem_b0, occurrence 2), taking precedence over its CLOCKED_BY storage. Not listed: acc_adr only indexes the array (SELECTS); cache_o.data only forwards host_req_i.data or bus_rsp_i.data to wdata_i (COPIES, lines 151, 236); cache_i.data only carries rdata_o to host_rsp_o.data (line 156); host_rsp_o is a transport record.

conceptual assets.concept: Cache directory -- the per-block valid flag and stored tag that say which address block a cache line holds
conceptual assets.reasoning: The lookup flow reads the flag and tag of the indexed block: `valid_mem_rd <= valid_mem(to_integer(unsigned(acc_idx)));` (line 387) and `tag_mem_rd <= tag_mem(to_integer(unsigned(acc_idx)));` (line 400), both tested by hit_o (line 405). Updates: reset (line 377), `if (clr_i = '1') then valid_mem <= (others => '0');` (lines 380-381), invalidation to '0' under inv_i (lines 382-383), allocation to '1' under new_i (lines 384-385) with `tag_mem(to_integer(unsigned(acc_idx))) <= acc_tag;` (lines 397-398), acc_tag being the tag bits of addr_i (line 366). Integrity: a block may count as present only after allocation for its tag and until invalidation or clear (lines 381-385, 398); a corrupted flag or tag makes the hit decision accept a block for another address or reject a held one. Availability is also established: the fence-clear and error-invalidation flows depend on these flags being cleared (lines 219, 255). In neorv32_cache the update commands originate from controller decisions: cache_o.cmd_clr in S_CLEAR (line 219, SELECTED_BY ctrl.state), cache_o.cmd_new in S_DOWNLOAD_REQ (line 226, SELECTED_BY ctrl.state), cache_o.cmd_inv when ctrl.buf_err = '1' in S_DOWNLOAD_DONE (line 255, GATED_BY ctrl.buf_err); each is computed here from a decision, so the sub-unit wiring exception holds. valid_mem, tag_mem and their registered read copies valid_mem_rd and tag_mem_rd store (CLOCKED_BY clk_i); clr_i, inv_i and new_i set (GATES valid_mem, occurrence 2); addr_i sets (SOURCES acc_tag, occurrence 2), the value stored into tag_mem. Not listed: acc_idx only selects the entry; acc_tag only carries the slice of addr_i (CARRIES tag_mem, line 398).

conceptual assets.concept: Cache hit decision -- whether the requested address is held in the cache
conceptual assets.reasoning: `hit_o <= '1' when (valid_mem_rd = '1') and (tag_mem_rd = acc_tag) else '0';` (line 405) computes the decision; it enters neorv32_cache as cache_i.sta_hit (line 286) and is tested in S_LOOKUP by `elsif (cache_i.sta_hit = '1') then` (line 189). On a hit a read is acknowledged with the cached word (lines 190-192) and a write updates the cached word (line 194); on a miss a read starts a block download (line 200). Integrity: the decision must follow the predicate of line 405; a wrong hit returns or overwrites cached data for an address that is not held, a wrong miss forces a download. hit_o is the exit port of neorv32_cache_memory (CONSTRAINED_BY tag_mem_rd and GATED_BY valid_mem_rd, occurrence 2). cache_i.sta_hit sets the decision in neorv32_cache through the connection from neorv32_cache_memory_inst.hit_o (occurrence 3), and this block tests it in an if (line 189), so the sub-unit wiring exception holds. valid_mem_rd, tag_mem_rd and acc_tag are operands of the condition, not its result.

conceptual assets.concept: Cache data write decision -- whether and which byte lanes of the addressed cache word are overwritten
conceptual assets.reasoning: On a write hit `cache_o.we <= host_req_i.ben;` (line 194, gated by cache_i.sta_hit, not ctrl.buf_dir and the write condition of line 190), during a download `cache_o.we <= (others => '1');` (line 237), and zero otherwise (line 150). In neorv32_cache_memory each byte lane is written only when its we_i bit is '1' (lines 413-423). Integrity: the cached word may change only on a write hit or a downloaded word (lines 194, 237); a wrong enable writes data into a block of another address or drops an update, leaving the cached word different from the bus write issued with it (line 195). When READ_ONLY is true, line 190 never takes the write arm, so cache_o.we is driven only at line 237. cache_o.we computes the decision (GATED_BY cache_i.sta_hit, occurrence 3) and originates it here, so the sub-unit wiring exception holds; we_i sets it in neorv32_cache_memory (GATES data_mem_b0, occurrence 2). host_req_i.ben is a field of a transport port and is not reported.

conceptual assets.concept: Cache controller state -- the step of the lookup, direct-access, clear and download sequence the controller is in
conceptual assets.reasoning: `case ctrl.state is` (line 164) selects every command and response: the record shows SELECTS from ctrl.state to bus_req_o.stb, cache_o.cmd_new, cache_o.cmd_clr, cache_o.we, host_rsp_o.ack and ctrl_nxt.state. The state is self-updating through ctrl_nxt.state (line 136, transitions at lines 169-265), stored by `ctrl <= ctrl_nxt;` on the rising edge (lines 125-126) and reset to S_IDLE (line 117). Integrity: each command is issued only in its state, for example cmd_clr only in S_CLEAR (line 219) and cmd_new only in S_DOWNLOAD_REQ (line 226); a corrupted state issues them out of sequence. Availability is also established: the machine returns to S_IDLE after each response (lines 192, 211, 221, 258) and the others arm recovers any other value (line 265). ctrl.state stores it: the map writes the clock edge only on the whole record ctrl (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 10, line 126) and the field has no occurrence on line 126, so the reset-arm occurrence of the same clocked process (occurrence 2, line 117) is cited with edge null; for the same missed statement the flow graph lists the field as constant-valued. ctrl_nxt.state computes the transition (GATED_BY ctrl.buf_sync, occurrence 3, line 169).

conceptual assets.concept: Direct-access decision -- whether a host access bypasses the cache and goes straight to the bus
conceptual assets.reasoning: In S_IDLE `if (unsigned(host_req_i.addr(31 downto 28)) >= unsigned(UC_BEGIN)) or (host_req_i.amo = '1') or (host_req_i.debug = '1') then ctrl_nxt.buf_dir <= '1';` (lines 171-173) decides the bypass; in S_LOOKUP `if (ctrl.buf_dir = '1') then` sends the access to the bus (lines 186-188) and the bus response is returned unchanged (line 209). Integrity: accesses at or above UC_BEGIN, atomic accesses and debug accesses must not be answered from or written into the cache (lines 186-196); a wrong decision answers them from cached data or writes them into the cache. ctrl_nxt.buf_dir computes the decision (GATED_BY host_req_i.addr, occurrence 3), defaulting to '0' every cycle (line 140). ctrl.buf_dir stores it for S_LOOKUP: it is stored by line 126, the map writes CLOCKED_BY only on the whole ctrl, so occurrence 2 (line 121) is cited with edge null. host_req_i.addr, host_req_i.amo and host_req_i.debug are fields of a transport port and are not reported.

conceptual assets.concept: Download block address -- the captured tag and index of the missed block and the word offset counted through it
conceptual assets.reasoning: In S_LOOKUP `ctrl_nxt.tag <= host_req_i.addr(31 downto 32-tag_size_c);` and the index (lines 180-181) are captured and the offset is cleared (line 182). During the download both the bus request and the cache write use `ctrl.tag & ctrl.idx & ctrl.ofs` with two zero bits (lines 225, 227, 235, 238), and `ctrl_nxt.ofs <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(ctrl.ofs) + 1);` advances on each bus acknowledge (lines 243-244) until `and_reduce_f(ctrl.ofs) = '1'` ends the block (line 245). Integrity: every downloaded word must come from, and be written to, the matching word of the requested block; a corrupted tag, index or offset fills the allocated line with another block's data or ends the download early. Availability is also established: the counter must reach the last word for the download to complete (lines 245-246). ctrl.tag, ctrl.idx and ctrl.ofs store these values (stored by line 126; the map writes CLOCKED_BY only on the whole ctrl, so occurrence 2 at their reset lines 122-124 is cited with edge null). ctrl_nxt.ofs computes the next offset (DERIVES_FROM ctrl.ofs, occurrence 4, line 244). Not listed: ctrl_nxt.tag and ctrl_nxt.idx only carry slices of host_req_i.addr; cache_o.addr only concatenates the stored parts into the sub-unit address input; bus_req_o is a transport port.

conceptual assets.concept: Download bus-error status -- whether any bus response of the current block download reported an error
conceptual assets.reasoning: `ctrl_nxt.buf_err <= ctrl.buf_err or bus_rsp_i.err;` (line 242) accumulates the errors of the download and S_LOOKUP clears it (line 183). In S_DOWNLOAD_DONE `if (ctrl.buf_err = '1') then` drives cache_o.cmd_inv, host_rsp_o.ack and host_rsp_o.err to '1' (lines 254-257), invalidating the block and reporting the error; otherwise the lookup is retried (line 260). Integrity: a block fetched with a bus error must not stay valid and must be reported as an error (lines 255-257); a lost flag leaves the block valid, so the retried lookup answers from it. ctrl_nxt.buf_err computes the error decision (GATED_BY bus_rsp_i.err, occurrence 4); ctrl.buf_err stores it (stored by line 126; occurrence 2, line 120, cited with edge null because the map writes CLOCKED_BY only on the whole ctrl); cache_o.cmd_inv computes the invalidation decided from it (GATED_BY ctrl.buf_err, occurrence 3). host_rsp_o.err is a field of a transport port and is not reported.

conceptual assets.concept: Pending access request -- a host access strobe held until the controller starts its lookup
conceptual assets.reasoning: `ctrl_nxt.buf_req <= ctrl.buf_req or host_req_i.stb;` (line 137) holds a host strobe until S_IDLE takes it with `elsif (host_req_i.stb = '1') or (ctrl.buf_req = '1') then` (lines 170-175), and S_LOOKUP clears it (line 184). Availability: a strobe that arrives while the controller is busy in another state must still start a lookup once the controller is idle (lines 137, 170, 175). Integrity is not claimed separately. ctrl_nxt.buf_req computes the next flag (GATED_BY ctrl.buf_req, occurrence 2); ctrl.buf_req stores it (stored by line 126; occurrence 2, line 118, cited with edge null because the map writes CLOCKED_BY only on the whole ctrl).

conceptual assets.concept: Pending fence request -- a fence held until the controller clears the cache
conceptual assets.reasoning: `ctrl_nxt.buf_sync <= ctrl.buf_sync or host_req_i.fence;` (line 138) holds a fence until S_IDLE takes it with `if (host_req_i.fence = '1') or (ctrl.buf_sync = '1') then ctrl_nxt.state <= S_CLEAR;` (lines 168-169), ahead of any pending access.
